skill.name: wiki-qa
skill.description: Answers questions about a code repository using source file analysis. Use when the user asks a question about how something works, wants to understand a component, or needs help navigating the codebase.
skill.summary: Answers repository questions with evidence from source files and inline citations.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code examples, not executable shell or Ruby syntax. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe instructions in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Use `##` headings, code blocks with language tags, tables, bullet lists

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 25 uses Markdown backticks to describe response formatting with headings and code blocks. It is prose in SKILL.md and does not execute a command.
Line 26 uses Markdown backticks around an example citation format. It is documentation text, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.

content.user_title: Answer Codebase Questions with Source Evidence
content.value_statement: Repository questions often require searching many files before the answer is clear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to answer from source evidence with inline citations.
actual_capabilities: Answers questions about files, functions, components, and repository behavior.
Searches the codebase for relevant source files before responding.
Reads source files and grounds answers in discovered evidence.
Provides inline file and line citations for claims.
Identifies key files and explains their roles in the answer.
limitations: It only supports answers that can be grounded in available source files.
It does not use external knowledge unless the repository contains it.
It may need more files when the codebase evidence is incomplete.
It is not a replacement for running tests or executing the application.

use_cases.title: Understand A Feature
use_cases.description: Trace how a feature works across related files and receive a cited explanation.

use_cases.title: Onboard To A Repository
use_cases.description: Ask where important behavior is defined and get a map of key files.

use_cases.title: Review Implementation Details
use_cases.description: Confirm how a component handles data flow, configuration, or errors from source evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Find Where Behavior Lives
prompt_templates.prompt: Where is [feature or behavior] implemented in this repository? Cite the files and lines that support your answer.

prompt_templates.title: Explain A Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how [component, class, or function] works. Include a key files table and cite source evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Understanding a specific part of the codebase

prompt_templates.title: Trace A Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace the flow for [user action or system event] from entry point to final result. Use only repository evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Implementation Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare how [option A] and [option B] are implemented in this repository. Explain tradeoffs supported by source citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis across related code paths

output_examples.input: How does authentication work in this repository?
output_examples.output: A concise explanation of the authentication flow, followed by a key files table and inline citations to the relevant source lines.

output_examples.input: Where is the payment retry logic defined?
output_examples.output: A direct answer naming the files that define retry behavior, with cited evidence and notes about any missing context.

output_examples.input: Explain how the API client handles errors.
output_examples.output: A source-grounded summary of error handling paths, including the functions involved and file references for each claim.

best_practices: Ask one focused repository question at a time.
Name specific files, features, or behaviors when possible.
Request citations when the answer will guide implementation decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for facts that are not present in the repository.
Do not rely on the answer as proof that tests pass.
Do not request broad architecture summaries without a clear focus.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It answers repository questions using source file analysis and inline citations.

faq.question: Does it run code?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructions focus on searching, reading, and explaining source files.

faq.question: Can it answer questions about any repository?
faq.answer: It can help when the needed evidence exists in files the agent can read.

faq.question: Why are citations important?
faq.answer: Citations let users verify claims against the exact source files and lines.

faq.question: Can it use external documentation?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the agent to use actual source files and avoid external knowledge.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, reviewers, and technical leads can use it to understand repository behavior.
